Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a massive right-sided pneumothorax with significant leftward mediastinal shift and abnormal cardiac positioning, which are characteristic radiographic signs of cardiac volvulus (herniation) into the empty right pleural space following extrapleural pneumonectomy for mesothelioma. This mechanical torsion of the heart and great vessels leads to acute haemodynamic compromise.
